summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, gastrostomy dependence, and chronic anemia, was admitted after outpatient labs revealed a hemoglobin of 6.5. He reported mild lightheadedness but denied chest pain, shortness of breath, or signs of acute bleeding. He received two units of packed red blood cells during the admission, with hemoglobin rising from 6.5 to 7.1 post-transfusion. His anemia was attributed to chronic disease, consistent with prior evaluations, and iron studies supported this diagnosis. He remained stable throughout the stay, with no complications from transfusions. His liver function was normal, immunosuppressive medications were continued, and chronic conditions were managed without change. He was discharged home with services, following up with the liver clinic for ongoing care.
